result:
Two findings, handled in order.

**1. Minor: the typo in the `round_price()` docstring.** I'll fix it. It's a docstring-only change with no behavior to test, so there is no RED step. `make test` still runs afterward.

<edit path="rates/card.py">
    '''Round a price to whole cents. A tie goes to the nearest even cent.'''
</edit>

**2. Important: switch to ROUND_HALF_UP.** I would not make this change. D2 is a decision from the owner, made at plan review: prices round half-even to match the ledger system. The reviewer's reason, "customers expect half-up", has no source in the spec or plan, and it contradicts a recorded decision. Under the executing-plans skill this is a ruling, not a stop. It is not destructive or security-sensitive, has no effect outside the worktree, and crosses no scope fence. So I keep the code as it is and ledger the ruling. The change is cheap to reverse later: one constant, plus the test that pins the tie behavior.

<command>
make test > .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log 2>&1; tail -n 15 .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log
</command>

If the tests pass, I commit the fix and append the ledger line in the same call:

<command>
git add rates/card.py && git commit -m "docs: fix typo in round_price docstring" && printf '%s\n' "Final review: fix pass — fixed docstring typo in rates/card.py (make test green)." "Ruling: kept ROUND_HALF_EVEN, declined reviewer's switch to ROUND_HALF_UP — plan Decision D2 (owner, 2026-11-02) requires half-even to match the ledger system, and the 'customers expect half-up' claim has no source in the spec — if wrong, customer-facing prices differ from half-up expectations on exact ties; fix is one constant plus the tie-case test." >> .sdd/14-rate-card/progress.md
</command>

I then continue with the plan-completion protocol and delete this plan's workspace. I do not call finishing-a-development-branch before the gate: a merge or push is a stop condition and needs your partner.

**Message to my partner:**

All tasks in `14-rate-card` are complete and `make test` passes. The whole-plan review returned two findings:

- **Docstring typo ("neerest"):** Fixed in `rates/card.py` and committed.
- **"Switch to ROUND_HALF_UP":** Declined. D2 in the plan says prices round half-even to match the ledger system, so I kept `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. I ledgered this as a `Ruling:` line. The reviewer's claim that customers expect half-up is unsourced. If that expectation is real, D2 needs to be revisited. Switching means changing the constant in `rates/card.py` and updating the tie-case test.

The branch is ready for your decision on merge or push, which I have not done.
